So, with Conference Championship weekend upon us, I thought I'd try and give my two cents about what went wrong with a Divisional Round loser. I might do other teams, depending on how people react to this. First up, the Green Bay Packers. Now, I'm a Cowboys fan, so I'm not too fond of the Packers after what happened in last year's playoffs and due to the historic rivalry between the Cowboys and Packers. So, I was rooting for the Cardinals. But, let's start the autopsy anyway. *Puts on surgical mask.* Scalpel.

Regular Season Record: 10-6

Head Coach: Mike McCarthy

Finished 2nd in the NFC North, 5th seed in NFC overall.

Let's begin with the Regular Season, since we need to put things into perspective, plus it's unfair to jump straight to the playoff game against Arizona. Oh, we'll get to that, don't you worry.

The Packers started out undefeated for their first six games. After a bye week, they played an away game against the also-then-undefeated Denver Broncos and lost 29-10. They then lost an away game against the Panthers. They returned home, only to lose a home game against the Lions, who had only won one game prior, **since *1991.*** While they won their next game, which was at the eventual NFC North champion Vikings, they went on to lose to the Bears at home. They quickly bounced back, beating the Lions at Ford Field, the Cowboys at Lambeau, and the Raiders at O.co Coliseum.

Then came the loss to Arizona. [Clip.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8h_layPYdLU)

No, not that one. We'll get to that. No, the regular season loss is what I'm referring to. In week 16, the Packers went down to Glendale, Arizona to face the Arizona Cardinals. They lost 38-8 in what was the worst loss in the Aaron Rodgers era. Despite losing, they clinched a playoff spot with the Giants losing earlier that day. The Pack then went back home in a winner-takes-all game for the division crown against the Vikings. This was a game so important to Green Bay that...they lost to the Vikings 20-13.

Now, onto the postseason. The Packers went on the road to Landover, Maryland, where they beat Washington 35-18.

And now, the moment you've all been waiting for: The playoff game against Arizona. And it's here we find the cause of death: Defensive Failure. Packers fans, please hear me out.

Let's begin by addressing the elephant brought into the room by my prognosis: Yes, Carson Palmer did throw two interceptions, whereas Aaron Rodgers threw only one. Also, the Packers were ahead briefly. However, please note that I'm not saying the Cardinals Defense played much better. Neither defense played particularly well. The fourth quarter was particularly insane. I bet that at least one Packers fan watching looked at their beer and going, "What the Hell is in this?" Heck, I asked that same thing about my soda.Then came Rodgers' game-tying TD. My roommate, who isn't really a fan of either team, freaked out at that point. But the Defensive Failure took root in overtime. I'm sorry, but if you allow a 75-yard pass on the first play of OT, and 391 yards passing plus 3 TDs overall, that's Defensive Failure. There's always next year.

So, what'd y'all think?
TL;DR: Packers got swept at home by teams in their division.

The Packers defense carried the team all year. The offensive line was banged up with backups playing and they weren't able to give Rodgers time most of the season. Which slowed down the offensive attack quite a bit. Along with losing our number 1 WR in the preseason. They need to bolster the line and things will be ok
